rationale: I read the complete held EO 12686 (54 FR 32629, Aug. 4, 1989): it establishes the President's Commission on Aviation Security and Terrorism (Pan Am 103), sets functions, a report within 6 months (sec. 2(b)), administration under DOT and FACA, and in sec. 4 provides that 'The Commission shall terminate 30 days after submitting its report to the President.' It has no savings clause. I read the held EO 12774 (56 FR 49833, Sept. 27, 1991), secs. 3-5: sec. 3, headed as revoking orders 'which established committees that have been terminated or whose work has been completed', lists '(b) Executive Order No. 12686, as amended by Executive Order No. 12705, establishing the President's Commission on Aviation Security and Terrorism', and sec. 5 makes the order effective Sept. 30, 1991. This is an express revocation of the whole order naming it by number, with no carve-out and no savings language. EO 12705 (March 3, 1990) extended the report deadline to May 15, 1990, so under sec. 4 the Commission would have terminated by its own term about 30 days after the report (the date the report was submitted is not held), which would be an earlier ending than the 1991 revocation; I did not use the report deadline as a basis and the sec. 4 own-term evidence is held only in an APP copy. The catalog note ('Amended by EO 12705; Revoked by EO 12774') and its candidate events agree but are leads; the basis is the held acting text. Provisional NO hypothesis only; the first-effective end date is left unresolved.
